slides.title: 5 plumbing myths that cost homeowners money

slides.myth: Ice cubes sharpen your garbage disposal blades.
slides.fact: Most disposals don't have sharp blades at all. Lugs on a spinning plate push food against a grinding ring. Ice may knock some stuck bits loose, but it doesn't sharpen anything.

slides.myth: Run hot water with the disposal to cut grease.
slides.fact: Use cold water. It keeps fats solid so they get ground up and flushed along. Hot water can let grease slide further down the pipes, where it can clog later.

slides.myth: A water heater needs no maintenance.
slides.fact: Sediment settles in the bottom of the tank over time and can cut efficiency and shorten its life. Plumbers recommend flushing it about once a year.

slides.myth: Drop-in tank tablets keep your toilet clean for free.
slides.fact: Plumbers say chlorine tablets can slowly wear out the rubber flapper and seals in the tank, and a shrinking tablet can jam the flush valve.

slides.myth: Pipes only freeze when the whole house is cold.
slides.fact: Pipes in garages, attics, crawl spaces and exterior walls can freeze even when the house is warm. On a hard-freeze night, open the cabinets under sinks and let a faucet drip.
slides.source: National Weather Service guidance via local news
